Title: Process for amplifying, detecting, and/or cloning nucleic acid sequences using a thermostable enzyme
AI_Human_Abstract: This technology describes a method for making millions of copies of specific DNA sequences using heat-resistant enzymes and temperature cycling. It's essentially the foundational process for PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction), which allows scientists to amplify tiny amounts of DNA for analysis and testing.
AI_Keywords: PCR machine, DNA amplification, genetic testing, DNA copying, molecular diagnostics
AI_Use_Cases: Medical diagnostics for detecting diseases like COVID-19 or genetic disorders | Forensic analysis for crime scene DNA evidence identification | Agricultural biotechnology for crop improvement and plant disease detection
AI_Market_Potential: This represents the core PCR technology which is fundamental to a multi-billion dollar molecular diagnostics market that continues to grow rapidly. The market remains highly relevant with expanding applications in personalized medicine, infectious disease testing, and biotechnology research.
Abstract: A process for amplifying any target nucleic acid sequence contained in a nucleic acid or mixture thereof comprises treating separate complementary strands of the nucleic acid with a molar excess of two oligonucleotide primers and extending the primers with a thermostable enzyme to form complementary primer extension products which act as templates for synthesizing the desired nucleic acid sequence. The amplified sequence can be readily detected. The steps of the reaction can be repeated as often as desired and involve temperature cycling to effect hybridization, promotion of activity of the enzyme, and denaturation of the hybrids formed.
